backlogged.summary: In the builder-changes commit, the pathspec `:(exclude,literal)<cache>` only leaves out the test-count cache. If a project already tracks that file, its modifications stay unstaged after the commit and the feature worktree is left dirty. The cache is now gitignored by `harness init`, but projects initialised earlier have no such entry.

The solo base re-run loop at the end of verify runs `runCommand` directly and does not go through the pool or check for an abort signal. A SIGINT during that phase is only noticed by whatever runs next. The same gap exists for the head solo re-run loop.

The AC-1, AC-2 and ES-1 tests use wall-clock polling: a 3 s wait for another run to be seen, an 8 s hang, and 5 s vacuity timeouts. They could be flaky on a heavily loaded CI host, as with B185 and B177.

A base run that timed out while overlapped is now re-run alone. A genuinely slow base check can therefore take up to twice `vacuity_timeout_sec`. This matches the SPEC wording but adds worst-case latency.

If .harness/runs/test-count-cache.json is already tracked on the base (it was committed before 3be2b83), the builder-commit pathspec exclude leaves its modification unstaged. The feature worktree then stays dirty after the builder commit, and nothing reports it. Consider `git rm --cached` or a warning when the cache is tracked.

The solo base re-run loop runs after the head retry loop but does not check the abort signal between iterations. A SIGINT during a long series of solo base re-runs relies on runCommand's own signal handling (via `run`), and every queued re-run is still started in turn.
The AC-3 test returns early on Windows (the fake git is a shebang script), so the failed-worktree-add cleanup path is exercised only on POSIX.
Timing-based fixture for AC-1/ES-1 (3 s polling window, 5 s vacuity timeout, 8 s hang) may flake on a heavily loaded CI host, similar to the existing F26 timing concerns.
